story: Noah, son of Lamech, was the tenth and last patriarch before the flood. Lamech had hoped his son would bring relief from toil upon the cursed ground. When Noah was five hundred years old, his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth were born. God, seeing the wickedness of mankind, resolved to destroy the earth with a flood, returning it to watery chaos. Noah alone found favor and was commanded to build an ark to save his family and every kind of land animal. Noah obeyed faithfully, and when the flood came, he, his family, and the animals were preserved while the rest of mankind perished. After the waters receded, Noah offered burnt offerings to God, who accepted them and made a covenant never again to destroy the earth by flood, setting a rainbow in the clouds as a sign. God blessed Noah and his sons, commanding them to be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth again. Certain laws were given: not to eat living animals, not to shed human blood, and other moral commands. Afterwards, Noah became a farmer and planted a vineyard. He drank of its wine, grew drunk, and lay uncovered in his tent. His son Ham saw his father's nakedness and told his brothers, who covered Noah without looking. When Noah awoke, he cursed Ham's son Canaan to be a servant to his brothers. From Noah's three sons came all the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
blind: The hero, son of an elder man, was the last patriarch before a great flood in a line of long-lived ancestors. His father had hoped his son would bring relief from toil upon a cursed ground. When the hero was five hundred years old, his three sons were born. A supreme deity, seeing the wickedness of mankind, resolved to destroy the earth with a flood, returning it to watery chaos. The hero alone found favor and was commanded to build a large boat to save his family and every kind of land animal. He obeyed faithfully, and when the flood came, he, his family, and the animals were preserved while the rest of mankind perished. After the waters receded, the hero offered burnt offerings to the deity, who accepted them and made a covenant never again to destroy the earth by flood, setting a rainbow in the clouds as a sign. The deity blessed the hero and his sons, commanding them to be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth again. Certain laws were given: not to eat living animals, not to shed human blood, and other moral commands. Afterwards, the hero became a farmer and planted a vineyard. He drank of its wine, grew drunk, and lay uncovered in his tent. One of his sons saw his father's nakedness and told his brothers, who covered him without looking. When the hero awoke, he cursed that son's child to be a servant to his brothers. From the hero's three sons came all the peoples that spread across the earth after the flood.
